They go to the very point that my friend complains about, and in my submission, without establishing this, he can argue about nothing because nothing has been established in terms of tendering the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This witness can depose about what was found in the premises of Mr. Mucic and Mr. Delalic and this is all he is saying. He is not talking about the contents of the document. These documents were found in those premises. Why can he not prove that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you remember in an earlier hearing we kept on emphasising that these twelve files can only be tendered by the person who identified them, and so designated them. This is why it is necessary to bring this witness to indicate the files which he so identified. I do not think the Prosecution is even insisting that the contents of the documents which he has so identified belong to a particular category, I do not think they are saying that. All they are saying is these items were those which were collected by Navrat from the INDA-Bau offices or Mucic's house and then when they were brought to the police station they were categorised by a certain officer, and this is the officer who categorised them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, without -- which one of us do you want to hear first? Ladies first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The Prosecutor has not proved what you are drawing our attention to. This witness, everything that has been done by this witness; he recognised the label with his handwriting. This witness is not a witness who took items from any space that could have perhaps been the origin of items related to Mr. Delalic. We have heard, and my colleague Mr. O'Sullivan this moment said before us, we have 800 pages of testimony of witnesses from the moment they entered any space where there could be any items related to Mr. Delalic, including these. Mr. Navrat has spoken about these items totally differently during his testimony, different to what the witness is saying today. Therefore, it is necessary for us to have the possibility of final arguments for the court to see once again the irregularity in the attempt until this day for items to be brought to this court and be presented as legal. In our law, there is a Latin proverb which says what is irregular and illegal from the beginning cannot become during the proceedings. Therefore, I would like to ask you and to repeat the argument of my colleague once again, this is not the time where we can discuss the admissibility of evidence. One witness recognises the colour, another one recognises the handwriting on a very small label. The content is not recognised by anyone. I would like to wait for the witness to be cross-examined and then after 1,000 pages of the transcript we can give our final decision, when the court will be able to make a fair and final decision. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object, your Honour, to counsel joining in these debates when it has nothing to do with this counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, as long as the Prosecution wants to stipulate that these documents are not admissible in any way against my client, either for inferences or anything else, then that is fine. If he is making a limited offer of these documents as only against some defendants and not against others, that is fine. Otherwise, if these documents are to have any admissibility or any use in evidence against my client, I believe I have standing to, in the words of Mr. Niemann, join into this. I represent Hazim Delic and if this evidence is to be used against Hazim Delic or used by the court in any way to determine Mr. Delic's guilt, innocence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, I see. There is a point there. If counsel is likely to be affected by admission of the document, he is entitled to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And insofar as counsel wishes to limit himself to that, your Honours, perhaps my objection was premature and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with that, I do not recall hearing any testimony today from Herr Panzer concerning the content of those documents. As I understood it, there was a limited offer from the Prosecution not to offer the contents of the documents. As I understand Mr. Panzer's testimony, all he testified to -- I may have missed something, if I did, I apologise -- he identified twelve file folders as opposed to any of the contents of those, so with that, as long as all they are trying to introduce is simply the orange, green and whatever, all rainbow coloured cardboard files, I do not know that we would have any objection to that. Once they start talking about the contents, that is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose that Delalic's counsel is extending the argument beyond what was presented. The witness did not, in any of the cases, indicate any contents of the labels he is giving to those documents. In the case of the files, the folders had nothing in them. There might be things in them, but he said nothing about anything in them. The argument now which Delalic's counsel is saying is that there should be a link between how he got these folders and how he indicated those identification marks. I think this has started all the way from Navrat and he brought it to the police office, and then all he did is try and identify them by the labels he put on them and this is the identification he is now telling us. What is in the folders, a particular document or not, he does not know and I think he is not testifying as to that. This is the position at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, one further point in this matter. I am holding the letter of 28th August 1997 sent to us by Mr. Niemann, in which he says: "At the conclusion of the evidence of Mr. Panzer, it will be the condition of the prosecutor that all the preconditions to admissibility are met." He then asks our advice as to whether we anticipate any objections and if we do, whether we have general objections, submissions to make on admissibility. He asked us to inform him whether we would be making such objections, making such argument and submission this morning. We told him we would, he agreed and that such argument to his attempt to tender would take place after Panzer and before or during Defence having an opportunity to present to your Honours our arguments based on the testimony of all these witnesses which covers hundreds of pages which is not simply -- it is contradictory in our position, there are many things that are inconsistent between witnesses, documents improperly prepared, things that appear and disappear. Your Honours, this is premature, the understanding this morning was that we would not proceed halfway through this person's testimony, that we would wait until the end of this week, which is what we agreed at 9.55 this morning and it is inappropriate procedurally for the Prosecutor to attempt to tender these limited number of items at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Frankly, I agree to you entirely as to the contents of these things being tendered. You know nothing about the contents, so there is no way of admitting them. The fact he organised the folders in that way, I do not see much of an objection to that, that he organised the folder in the way it has been. This is all I think his testimony leads to.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: In our submission, that certainly does not satisfy any burden of proof as to whether or not these items are admissible. This is premature to attempt to admit these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Which are the items to be admitted? The documents or the folders?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is my friend admitting the folders or their contents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is the question I expected. What is being admitted? Is it the folders as they are, or the contents of those folders?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For about the third time, your Honour, we are merely seeking to tender the folders, not their contents. We are not asking any inferences to be drawn and it arises because counsel are insisting we prove chain of custody. This is a process that one ordinarily goes through when one proves chain of custody and we are endeavouring to do it. We are not asking that the contents of the documents be tendered at all. It merely proves they came in this form. While I am on my feet, perhaps I might proceed. This notion, your Honours, that seems to be created here that one does not tender something during the course of the evidence of a witness is frankly, in my submission, unheard of. The idea that counsel can have the luxury of hearing all Prosecution witnesses, evidence-in-chief, cross-examination, re-examination and then wait until all the witnesses have ended is something unheard of. Something similar of that has been provided for your Honours in rule 73.3, which permits the preliminary objection to be taken by motion prior to trial in relation to the exclusion of evidence obtained from the accused or having belonged to the accused. I suggest, your Honours, that if the Defence had availed themselves of the provisions of the rules in order to do that at an appropriate and opportune time, the idea of being able to argue the whole matter en masse may well have been available to them. They did not take advantage of the rules as they are provided, so they cannot now come along and complain that they are being deprived of an opportunity to argue the matter in a global sense. They have to be content with dealing with them document by document. Insofar as the letter that has been referred to, yes, I wrote a letter to them. Considering that counsel chose not to rely on the provisions of 73.3, in order to deal with this matter as a preliminary motion, I wrote to counsel in an effort to see how agreement could be reached between the Prosecution and the Defence on these issues in order not to labour the court with the tedious and long drawn out process of having to produce these documents one at a time. The only response I got to that, notwithstanding the fact that I asked to be given a letter in reply this morning, was; leave it until the end of the week and we will deal with it then. That is fine, your Honours, and in relation to some of the documents that is exactly what I intend to do. There is a large bundle of documents I will seek to tender at the end of the week because it seems to me to be inappropriate to have Prosecution witnesses sitting around waiting to give their evidence while we argue points of law on the admissibility of each particular document, the documents we allege came from these particular folders. In our submission, counsel can certainly argue those points then. These particular documents are documents peculiarly relative to this witness. This is the witness that received them and he placed his label on them. Seeing that they are tendered for the very limited purpose of establishing the chain, in my submission, there can be no objections to their admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Admissibility to the extent they were found in the premises occupied by the two accused. Nothing beyond that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought my explanation was fairly clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do apologise to my distinguished colleague, he does not know this because he joined the trial later, but the Defence for Mr. Delalic has submitted a request to the court denying the validity of these documents and their admissibility. Therefore, objection regarding all the cases before the court stands in accordance with the instruction of the court for the admissibility to be discussed, once the evidence is discussed. Therefore regarding the question raised, we are asking to be given the possibility for final argument regarding all the evidence. As for the concrete situation, and also regarding Rule 73 as well as Rule 95 in that respect, I believe that the court would allow us after 1,000 pages of the transcript and several witnesses heard to give our final arguments regarding the legality of the proceedings and the relation from the moment the document is seized until it arrives here and the admissibility of every individual piece of evidence. I would like to emphasise that during the hearing with Mr. Delalic in August, at my objection that my defendant is being shown documents allegedly seized during the search, Ms. McHenry said at the time that that was not used for that purpose and Defence did have the right to question the admissibility of evidence once it is offered to the court, using the American term, that issues are discussed once you step on to the bridge. As for the identification of the cases of items that the Prosecutor is trying to tender and request a decision of the court, I believe that also regarding the fact that the witness spoke about today, we have totally contradictory statements of witnesses before the court. Everything this witness confirmed was that the sticker in a corner of this folder was in his handwriting and we have heard several witnesses until now that stickers have been placed and have vanished, that stickers can be easily removed and moved on to other items. Previously, this witness has not identified in any way even the folder that the sticker with this handwriting is on. I do not want to give my final arguments now, but all that justifies our request that the admissibility of evidence, even what the statement has just said before the court, cannot be decided on now, that is premature. Until we show the court once again everything that has happened from the moment a third party seized an item, who and how brought it to the police station and who and when placed stickers on it and where items were kept. All those facts have -- there are different statements from different witnesses on all those items. We cannot be absolutely certain because we have a witness in front of us, that everything he said can be a basis for a decision to be made that everything is exactly as we have just heard it. I am appealing once again that admissibility of all the evidence is discussed after the cross-examination of the witness and after the final arguments have been presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Counsel appears to be putting two quite different issues. What the Prosecution is now putting forward before the Trial Chamber is admissibility of the folders which this witness identified as created by him. He was the one who made the folders and labelled them. You are insisting on the question of the contents of these folders which might be admitted into evidence when it comes to be argued. Definitely that is not the issue now. The issue is not a question of any documents, the issue is whether the folders which were collected by Navrat and brought to the office was kept by this witness who is identifying them as the folders which he kept. That is all the Prosecution is trying to show.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have some observations but I see it is 1.00 and I remember your Honour saying as we started this part that you were going to rise at 1.00. May I make those observations at the end of the luncheon adjournment please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I thought we had finished the last sentence. We will break now and come back at 2.30. (1.05 pm) (Adjourned until 2.30 pm) 20 21 22 23 24 25 (2.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can you invite the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps, your Honour, while the witness is returning, may I mention something? It seems I was given some incorrect information in relation to the filing of a Rule 73 motion. It would seem that such a motion was filed, though it is imprecise as to what the final outcome of that was and what argument was mounted in relation to it. Insofar as I said that a motion had not been filed, I was wrong in that and I apologise to the court and to Madam Residovic. Your Honours, while I am on my feet, it was mentioned by Mr. O'Sullivan that I had written a letter saying that I would not deal with the exhibits until after the conclusion of Mr. Panzer's evidence. Your Honours, the letter is quite precise in saying specific exhibits 109 to 147C. It makes no reference whatsoever to Exhibit 166 which is the exhibit we are now seeking to deal with. Lest there be any confusion about the matter, whilst this witness is in the witness box, and because of the specific evidence he will give in relation to four videotapes, I will be seeking to tender those and I put the Defence on notice of that, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had thought when we started this morning that you had announced we would argue the Witness R motion at 2.30 today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We still will. Actually, we are minded first in admitting the twelve folders under the rule of this chain of custody, because I think the chain of custody was properly established. All the Prosecution is saying and I still remember him and the witnesses is that they are tendering the folders not the contents in respect of the witness himself. He is the one who was in charge of those folders and it is he who is now tendering it in evidence. It could be admitted for that purpose: you can still invite him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber notes the objection of the Defence. They can raise whatever objections they would wish to at a time when the documents in the folders are being tendered. They can also in their final submissions still object to it and put whatever arguments they would want to. Even finally on appeal they can still raise it, if the judgment relies on those documents as evidence. You are still free, you are open at any stage to rely on arguments which you are putting on, but definitely we will admit it in evidence for this purpose. You are not inhibited from whatever you want to do with your objections. You understand what I have said? You are free at all stages to raise the argument that you pose to the admission of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have understood what you said and I have understood that perhaps I should not be presenting some of the arguments, but before I left this courtroom I had also understood that you had given the possibility to my colleague Mr. Greaves to give arguments for the same issue for the chain of custody, and in that respect I wanted to offer some more arguments before you make a decision. We did not believe that you would be doing during the recess, but I would like to ask you, your Honour, to tell you precisely exactly what time can the Defence of Mr. Delalic present its arguments related to the incomplete chain of custody, which is something that we have heard so many witnesses on and we have been working on this for three months; and secondly, when would we be able to ask you, if this witness identified his own label and packaging, the folder, to ask the Prosecutor for everything that is in the folder to be presented to us at this time and then give our objections to the content, because I can be neither wise enough nor informed enough to know every detail that we have discussed in the past three months. My remark not to judge things in advance this morning, that we should be expressing ourselves clearly, I do not wish by defending the interests of my client at any time to think that by offering us the frame and the label that this witness placed not on the spot but at a certain time later in the police station, that that could be any indication that something that is in that document did not come from somewhere else. Just one more thing: the Defence will prove that those materials contain things from Munich and from Bosnia because the letter the Prosecutor has just referred to, there are four pieces of evidence that were given to Mr. Delalic during his interviews, those are not documents coming from Vienna. That is why we believe that without analysis and without arguments for everything the witnesses have said, the chain of custody nor what the witness has said here can be accepted integrally. Another question: if we are accepting something in advance, why should the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I have the intention of arguing this issue. Before we went on break, what I was reacting to was Mr. Greaves' reminder that we intended to close at 1.00. When we resumed what we initially had in mind was the question of argument on the application for protective witnesses. This is what we had and this was what I stated in the morning when we resumed. What I have just told you about arguments is that all the Prosecution is trying to show is that this witness, Panzer, was responsible for these folders. He was not talking about the contents of the folders. If what you are arguing is the legality of the folders, the chain of custody of them, obviously there is clear evidence that he handled these folders and these were the folders he handled. There is nothing wrong in his telling the Trial Chamber these were the folders he handled. But when it comes to introducing evidence as to documents in those folders, then you have a right to challenge whatever, the legality of those things. At this stage, you really have no problem, except assuming that the moment the folders have been admitted, everything goes with it. It does not. This is what I am saying. At every stage you can still challenge whatever documents are in these folders if it is intended to use them against you. I think that is the position. It is not final, you can still challenge it later. Let us invite the witness. Let us take the application for ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Turone, my colleague would like the bench, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I sit down may I ask: after that, do we have the possibility for cross-examination with the witness for the chain of custody, and after that to ask you to change the decision that you have just made. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has not completed his evidence. When you examine him, you will find out whatever you think are the flaws in his chain of custody, if there are any. Yes, Mr. Turone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. First of all, we confirm that we are now in the position to definitely clarify that we withdraw any request of protection concerning Witness S, since the Prosecution is not going to call this witness any more. On the other hand, the Prosecution maintains the request of protection for Witness R. Actually, there are two different motions concerning Witness R, both filed on 22nd July, a motion seeking leave to call this witness and a motion for his protection from the public and the media. It is not very clear from the transcript of 7th August whether the leave for Witness R was already implicitly granted in the ruling of that day concerning a group of new witnesses, but since formally maybe the leave was not yet granted -- anyway, it is not clear to me whether it was already implicitly granted or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Because on that day you were not too sure whether it was R or S. It was not easy to make any decision on either -- you were not sure about the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We filed a motion to seek leave for calling Witness R on July 22nd. I believe that this motion was not yet decided even implicitly in the ruling, in the later ruling given on 7th August. This is why I would illustrate this motion too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you remember, that day there was argument between you and the Defence about who that particular witness was. You have given several names about this certain witness. It was not set.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: It was not set, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Witness R has very recently informed the office of the Prosecutor that he is willing to testify. He is a relevant witness for a number of counts, a number of killings and the count of inhumane treatment, and the Prosecution provided the Defence with the identity of witness R who was detained in the Celebici camp. Moreover, in November 1996, the Prosecution provided the Defence counsels with unredacted copies of the statement made by Witness R to the Office of the Prosecutor. The reason for which we seek leave to call this witness is that a number, a relevant number of Prosecution witnesses have decided not to testify in this trial, and so we did not think Witness R to be absolutely necessary when we filed our witness list on March 7th, but now the Prosecution deems that this witness becomes important because of the witnesses we lost in the meantime, and we reapproached the witness in the meantime, and the witness is now willing to testify. Your Honours know that there have been a number of circumstances such that we had to seek leave to call other witnesses, we are still trying to figure out which of our past witnesses will and will not testify. On the other hand, as your Honours ruled already, what is the root of contention in this issue is the Prosecution's compliance with the disclosure obligations and the OTP statement was disclosed in November 1996 and the intention to call this witness, Mr. R as a witness, was also made clear more than one month ago. About the request of protective measures concerning Witness R, we previously filed a number of requests for confidentiality for a number of witnesses. Witness R would have been in that group, but at that time Mr. R had not agreed to be a witness in this trial. Only recently, as I said, he reported to OTP that he is willing to testify, but he fears reprisals for his testimony, particularly after the recent publication of the Prosecution witness list in a Bosnian newspaper, so he requested the lowest level of protection, which is protection from the media and the public. It is the submission of the Prosecution that there is a need to consider the different psychological approaches of the different witnesses, witnesses being particularly sensitive and vulnerable, maybe stressed by the fact itself of seeing the Prosecution witness list published with unpleasant comments in the daily newspapers, so this is the reason for which we insist that these protective measures be granted to Mr. R. The trial, as we had already to consider many times, would not become a secret trial anyway because Mr. R would anyway testify in open session, only with face distorted and a pseudonym. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any opposition to this?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, your Honours. I get the translation much later, so I was waiting to hear exactly what Mr. Turone said. That is why I have been standing and keeping quiet for a couple of minutes and I apologise. I should like to ask the Trial Chamber and my learned colleague the Prosecutor to give us a list of all the protected witnesses, because last time we saw that there was a certain degree of confusion. Some protected witnesses renounced their protection, others insisted on it, so that actually we do not have complete insight into all the witnesses that need to be protected, and this is very important so that we can respect those protective measures. I am saying this because this morning when the request was made for protection of Witness R, in the translation we heard "witness A", so you see, all this would facilitate the proceedings. As for the proposals themselves that were made, I understand the need of the Prosecution, given the circumstances, to provide witnesses who would confirm the allegations of the Prosecution. However, my learned colleague Mr. Turone has just informed us that there will be a number of -- that a certain number of witnesses who were on the list refused to testify in this court, so this is one of the reasons why this witness who was not on the list is being offered. The Prosecution has so far informed us that only two witnesses out of a list of 66 will not come to testify in the Trial Chamber, and if that is correct, and if the Prosecutor will have to provide additional witnesses, could the Prosecution please inform us of this larger number of witnesses who were on the list, but who will not be coming to testify, so that the Defence need not necessarily waste time preparing for witnesses who will obviously not be coming. That is as far as the general arguments are concerned. As for this particular witness, regarding the statement he made to the Prosecution more than a month and a half ago, I accept that the court will assess all the elements appropriately and pass the proper ruling. I would also like to ask the Prosecution, regarding Witness S: is this a witness that the Prosecution does not wish to call or is it a witness who has refused to testify since this is a witness from whom the Defence took a statement before the Prosecution and informed the Prosecution about it; then the Prosecution took a statement from this same witness and put him on the list. As far as the Defence of Delalic is concerned, it is irrelevant who will provide the witness, because it is important that they tell the truth, that is all. So I am asking again whether it is the Prosecution that has decided not to call this witness or is it the witness himself who has decided not to come. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We have no difficulty in telling the Defence counsel that in this particular case of Mr. S, the Prosecution decided not to call the witness. From the other hand, for the other request of our learned colleague on the Defence, we sent to Defence lawyers a letter on August 22nd providing -- making available a list of all protected witnesses with names and letters. This list is available to all Defence lawyers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Her point is slightly different. What she says is a number of witnesses are being dropped and they should be informed about the names of those persons so they do not waste time working on the statements of those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We will inform the Defence lawyers about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Those witnesses whom you no longer wish to pursue, that is what she means.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The witnesses who refuse to testify, refuse to come, so that the Defence lawyers might know exactly which witnesses not to prepare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Whom you do not want to examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Even also, both the ones who do not want to come, for being afraid or any other reason, and the ones we decide not to call.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: How do you know these things until they actually refuse?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Actually we do our best in order to inform the Defence lawyer as soon as we receive information that a witness is not coming, refuses to come. This sometimes happens in a very sudden way as it was, for instance, for the two witnesses we had to examine through video link, they notified that they were not willing to testify any more in the very days in which we were preparing the testimony and the hearing, but I emphasise that we will do all our best in order to inform the Defence lawyers as soon as possible of the witnesses who, for any reason, are not going to testify immediately when we know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect to the Prosecution, I know they have their witness problems. At this point there are about as many characters here as in War and Peace. It would be very helpful to me if the Prosecution would take its witness list of March 7th or whatever date it was, take a look at that witness list, take off the names of the people they are not going to call, put on the names of the people they are going to call, put a pseudonym next to the ones they are going to have a pseudonym for, so that we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I see your point, you are saying that for those who the Prosecution do no longer want to call, they can be sure of those ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: But those who might refuse to attend when they are called, they cannot be sure of those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: I understand that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: They can perhaps give you the list of those who they no longer want to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: What I would respectfully request is the reverse of that, just give us a list of who they want to call. For instance, there is an expert witness they designated, a retired officer in the Dutch army. I believe the Prosecution is not going to call that man. I do not know that, I have just heard that. It would be nice to know. That is the type of thing I am suggesting, your Honours. I am not asking for the world and I understand that there is going to be times when something happens, with these two video link witnesses is, I guess, the best example, at the last minute somebody says no, I am not going to do it. At this Tribunal, we cannot send out the marshals and bring the witnesses down in handcuffs. I understand the Prosecution's problems in that and I am sympathetic to them. On the other hand, if they could be sympathetic to us, I have four file boxes full of documents and at some point it would be a whole lot easier to get rid of those documents and get it down to one document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think this should not be too difficult for them to -- when they make up their mind they will not call a witness, they can inform the Defence about that. I think that is easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think what we are after is a definitive list of what the Prosecution knows today about its witnesses. We understand entirely that they are going to get taken by surprise from time to time by someone who says I am not coming for whatever reason, or I cannot come for whatever, we understand that entirely, but if they know now that somebody is not coming it is going to save us all a lot of time and wasted effort in looking at those witnesses' statements in the future. That is what we are after, a definitive list of what they know now. I see my learned friend has risen probably to acknowledge that is what we are all after.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: If I may add something. I would like to emphasise that we do our best and we will try to do better. For instance, there are some witnesses right now we are not even -- they disappear. We are trying to find where they are. They gave us the information about their being willing to testify, but now they disappear and they -- so there are situations like that, this is why we have some difficulties, but we assure Defence lawyers that we do our best to inform as soon as possible whenever a real information about a witness coming or not coming will be in our possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, no one I think is questioning the good faith of the Prosecution. I acknowledge that they have behaved in a professional manner throughout this entire trial, it is just a matter of -- there is a dribble of information here and a drab of information there and if we could just get it all put together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose what you are requesting is not a difficult point. If the Prosecution has made up its mind not to call a particular witness, they inform you. For those where they have not made up their mind, they do not have to tell you. They can wait for the person. I do not see the problem about it. It is only those you are sure you are not calling, then you tell the Defence that. For all those which are borderline, you still wait until you make up your mind not to call them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to repeat the same as colleague Turone has just said, that a certain number of witnesses have said they would not come, so we are just asking that we are given the names of those witnesses, this number of witnesses, so that we should not waste time preparing for their statements. So far we know only about Witness S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We are still on the question of the protection. You have not reacted to the particular application.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will react to that. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that is what we wanted to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I have said nothing today so let me very briefly enter this discussion. When this case started, I understand that we all had a list of witnesses that the Prosecution expected to call. The court had it, the Defence counsel had it, we all had it and we had a definable universe. We are in the position now, all of us over here, of not knowing whether the Prosecution intends to put on ten more witnesses or twenty more witnesses or forty more witnesses. What I would really like to have is not any kind of a final decision by the Prosecution but they must have a working list similar to the one that we had on March 7th. If they could just give us a list "these are the witnesses we intend to call between now and the end of this trial", with the understanding that some of them may decide not to come, that will let us know what the universe is in terms of planning our cross-examination of those witnesses, but trying to get our own cases prepared in a manner that would allow us to start the Defence cases reasonably close to the time that the Prosecution ends theirs. Boil it all down, that is probably what we are asking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It appears there is no objection to the application for the protection of Witness R. All the others I think you can take care of it, giving them your list of witnesses, those you know you are likely to call.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: We will do our best, your Honour, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we now have the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Might the witness be recalled? I take it from what fell from your Honour immediately after we returned from luncheon adjournment that your Honours have admitted Exhibit 166?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, with the limitation that it is just the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is understood, your Honour. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Panzer, you said earlier in your evidence today that you had dealt with the videotapes that you had received from Mr. Mucic's apartment, the four videotapes, in a similar way that you had dealt with the twelve folders. I ask that the witness now be shown the four videotapes which are Exhibit 109, 110, 111 and 112. Mr. Panzer, the first one you have there in your hand, do you see on that video anything that causes you to recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This video is one I recognise on the basis of the label and the sticker, which I put on there. That is my writing on there. On the first line, it says "Celebit" that I recognise. There were two videotapes that we found at Mr. Mucic's apartment that had such a reference. One of them said "Celebit", and the other one said "Celebici" on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that one of the videotapes you had inserted into the video recorder and examined when you were at the premises of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a look at all four videotapes. They were put in the VCR and I had a look at them. M1D, that tape, I believe, has the footage where Mr. Mucic can be seen together with other people in uniform. They are in a room and there is some singing and drinking going on there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is one of the four videos that was actually handed to you by Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the label that you identify or see on the video that causes you to recognise, is there writing on that label?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean by label?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The label or the sticker on the video that you recognised it by.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are two stickers that have been put on here. These are the ones I put on. I put them on and I wrote on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The smaller of the stickers, what is written on the one that you have in your hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure I know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The small sticker that you put on the video that you now have in your hand, what is written on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are these two small stickers, it says M for Mucic, 1 for the listing system and then D, meaning that this is the fourth of the four videos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now would you look at the next video, please -- perhaps look through them and you might give them to us in their correct order, that is A, B, C. Starting with the one with A on it, would you look at that one, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have had a look at them, because I did not understand that there was not a sticker on here, but I see that there is a sticker here under this small note, because I put a sticker both on the tape as well as on the box. This tape is one I recognise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is written on the sticker? Can you see the sticker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise this sticker on the basis of what is written here, Velija, that is a name I remember and I recognise it on account of this sticker here, which I put. M1A, M for Mucic, 1 for the tape and A because this is the first tape that was seized.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a tape that you played at the premises of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this tape as well, just very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a tape that was handed to you by Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is one of the tapes that Mr. Mucic handed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the next one in order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So, this is the right one here. I can remember this tape as well, for two reasons. First of all because of the word written here, "Celebici" that is written on there, and then secondly because of this sticker, M1B. I wrote that on here and I put the sticker on the tape and then the case has the same sticker, M for Mucic, 1 for the tape and B because it is the second tape that we seized. As I said, with regard to these four tapes, I did not number them 1, 2, 3, 4; rather M for Mucic, 1, I put that on all for tapes and then I made the differentiation on the basis of the letters A, B, C and D for each of the tapes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that one of the videos that you had inserted in the video recorder and played while you were on the premises of Mr. Mucic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, just briefly also, and this is also a tape that was handed me by Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the next and final number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This tape is one I remember, not on account of the label but rather on account of the sticker I put on here, M1C, once again M for Mucic, 1 because it is a tape and C because this was the third tape. As you can see, I put a sticker with the same reference on the case of the tape and this is also a tape that was handed to me by Mr. Mucic and one that I had a brief look at in his apartment in his VCR.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I ask that those tapes be now handed to the technicians in the booth in order that they might be played one after the other on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it would be helpful to the record, if these are going to be Prosecution's 109 to 112, if we got in the record in some way whether Prosecution 109 is M1A or M1B or M1C. I think that would make the record somewhat clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am happy to oblige my friend with that your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Another thing, he said briefly viewed, how long each tape, a minute, two minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Hopefully it will be just a few moments each tape, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Are moments extending? What period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have not mentioned the time, but a total of ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How long did he watch of each tape?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is just merely to recognise the tapes or to have a fairly good view of the contents?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will be seeking to do two things, your Honours. Firstly for him recognise -- your Honours, what I will be seeking to do with the witness is to have him identify as he has seen them, which will take, as I understand it, a few seconds, but as I indicated earlier I will be seeking to tender these videos now and I will be seeking to play so much of them as is necessary to show their relevance, but from either event, it is very short. I am not going to labour the court with the whole viewing of the whole videos which would take, as I understand it, a few hours. I expect the whole process to be over in ten minutes in total, but I will be showing it for both purposes. I do have a transcript of them which I can make available.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise once again. Though this is not evidence that may have direct bearing on Mr. Delalic, but after this witness has identified his markings on the tapes and after all of us having heard that he briefly viewed very short segments, I do not know what will be shown, whether this insert seen by the witness or something else that he watched much later and analysed, and when things were changing so much from the moment of seizure to this moment when he sees, for instance, that a label is missing on one of his tapes, I really do not know whether in the name of identification, we are actually again admitting these exhibits as evidence. In my system this is quite different, but to me this appears like prejudicing the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one concern. Apparently, these tapes contain perhaps as much as an hour of video in each tape. I do not think the court can make a ruling about the relevancy of what is contained on the tapes by looking at three or four minutes of a tape because as I understand these tapes, they are vignettes that have a lot of different things on them. If what Mr. Niemann wants to do is let you see five minutes of a tape which is relevant and based upon that five minutes being relevant introduce in the record of this case an additional 55 minutes that may be totally irrelevant, then I think we all would have a substantial objection to that. If what Mr. Niemann believes is that there are only five minutes on each tape that are relevant to the issues in this case, then it seems to me extracts should be made from those tapes and the extracts admitted, but to judge relevance of a 60 minute tape on a five minute segment of it seems to me to be impossible and relevance, of course, is important in terms of what gets into this record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I did not understand him to mean that. Here is a witness who is in control of certain tapes. He made his markings on them and they have been played, he has viewed the tapes, so he should be made to say whether these are the same tapes which were viewed at the time when he had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I agree with that. If that is all that is being done, I have no objection. I understood he wanted to play part of them to show the entire tape was relevant. I cannot imagine that would work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was seeking to tender them for both purposes now, to play them for the purpose of this witness's identification of them and then to play a segment of them for the purposes of identification. Your Honours, the whole tape will be tendered, so it is not as though -- if there is any argument of completeness going on here then in my submission, your Honour, the whole tape is available and the Prosecution is not selectively trying to produce to the court as an exhibit a redacted version of the tape, hence be confronted with an objection by the Defence that we are trying to put forward only those parts which we say suit our case and not the Defence's. Conversely, your Honours, I do not believe that it is ever incumbent upon a party who has a video, a film, a document or any other to be precluded from tendering the whole document and reliance being only put on part of it. In numerous incidences, for example invoice books in a fraud case, there may be only three invoices in a bound volume which are relevant to the case. For all sorts of reasons the Prosecution may tender the whole book as an exhibit in the proceedings, but only seek to draw attention to three of the invoices. If another party seeks to rely on parts of the invoices which have not been raised by the Prosecution, well and good, that is available to them to do that. But in my submission, your Honour, I know of no rule which says that you have to proceed to extract all that is relevant. What I am trying to do is to achieve efficiency. It seems to me, your Honours, that we could sit here and listen to tapes -- I believe there is 17 hours in total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: There might be some difficulties in this one because here the witness is only saying that these are the tapes he received and not what they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But there are two issues your Honour that I would have thought it was necessary for me to demonstrate if I am to tender them for contents. The two issues are firstly his identification of them because he has identified the case but it is necessary to go further, I would have thought and to have him identify the actual video film itself because the case itself is probably not sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose that is when the issue of the contents arises. That is not the issue at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, but at the same time they are there and for the sake of efficiency, having regard to the fact that I submit that there could hardly be any argument about the chain of evidence in relation to the testimony this witness has given so far concerning these particular four tapes; these tapes were given to him by Mr. Mucic. He had them, he took them back, he labelled them, he played them, he saw them, and how could it possibly be argued that the chain of evidence is anything but complete? The next step, your Honours, is to seek to tender them as an exhibit in the proceedings. The chain of evidence may be satisfied to your Honours' satisfaction, but it may not be satisfied in terms of relevance. All I am seeking to do, your Honours, is while the videos are being played is to address both issues for the sake of efficiency, firstly to deal with the question of the chain and him identifying the tape as the one that was shown to him by Mr. Mucic. The second issue, your Honours, is while the tape is in the booth, in the machine, to play them so I can address the question of relevance and then seek to proceed to tender them. In my submission, your Honours, if your Honours do not wish me to do that I do not mind, but it seems to me an efficient way to go about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, I would prefer you to confine yourself to the chain of custody issue on the tapes. When the issue arises on the contents of the tape, you might be able to do that, because you might not be able to do it through him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honours please, I am happy to tender them as part of the chain of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think that is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I address your Honour as a matter of relevance please? My learned friend has said he is going to play only those parts of the tapes which are relevant. It follows from that that there are large parts of the tapes which are not relevant. What he is trying to do is to admit effectively evidence which is not relevant and, of course, Rule 89 says "only that evidence which is relevant may be admitted". Therefore those parts which he says are not relevant are going to be admitted by his producing these items. It seems to me he has some difficulty there. He may well talk about efficiency but he has also to remember Rule 89 as well. In my submission, Rule 89 takes precedence over efficiency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What we think he should do now is to show that these are the tapes which this witness had and which he took from Mr. Mucic. I think that is all he need do at this stage. If there is any other issue which arises as to the relevance of these tapes to whatever evidence he wants to give, he might at that stage bring that in, but not at this stage when all he is saying is he got these tapes from Mr. Mucic, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will proceed accordingly, your Honour, to deal with them only on the basis of the chain. Might the four videotapes be taken to the booth, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, while that is being done, I think Mr. Niemann said he was going to recite into the record some kind of cross-reference so we know which Prosecution exhibit equals M1A, B, C and D.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am happy to do that. M1A, your Honour, is Exhibit 109. M1B is Exhibit 110. M1C is Exhibit 111, and M1D is Exhibit 112. Your Honour, there is a series of translated transcripts that are attached which are given the numbers 109a, 110A et cetera, in that order, but it is the videotapes that we are concerned with at this stage. Now that the videos have been handed to the booth, might we start, your Honour, with the first one, which is Exhibit 109? I have prepared a transcript, your Honours, but seeing as we are dealing with it only on the basis of this witness identifying it for the chain of evidence, I do not think it is necessary to trouble your Honours with the transcript. Mr. Panzer, I want you to, when the people in the technician's booth are ready, I want you to look at your video monitor in front of you and if you see anything you recognise there, can you please say so and at that stage I will ask that the tape be stopped and which will move on to the next one. Would you please watch what you are shown? The moment you recognise, if you recognise anything at all, can you please say so. Might be start with 109, which is video M1A?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we hope that the Prosecutor is not showing this tape with the sound, because as far as I understand, the witness does not speak Bosnian and when he was watching it, he did not have a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not know how my friend is aware of that, but nevertheless I do not mind whether the sound is turned on or off. I assume the sound was turned on, and the fact that it is in a language the witness may or may not know, and I am not sure that is established, one can still identify language notwithstanding the fact that one does not speak it. I have no problem with that, your Honour, if they want to turn it off. There is more to sound than simply language, your Honour, there is music.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not think that is the issue at this stage. He just should identify what he saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But he could have heard as well your Honour, there could be sounds like music, cars braking, all sorts of things he might recognise which do not necessarily relate to what is said. Mr. Panzer, would you now please look at your screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I hope the witness understands we are not having an extensive viewing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have anything on my screen here, it is all dark. Oh, here it comes. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps your Honours, we can ask the booth to fast forward. It may be quicker to deal with it that way. Mr. Panzer does not seem to recognise anything so far, so if it could be fast forwarded through and he sees something he recognises we might stop at that stage. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: All we want to know is whether these are the tapes he viewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is what we want to do. There are parts of it which he now remembers, as I understand it, which he did not remember before. Perhaps if it could be fast forwarded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I put a question to you, Prosecutor? This tape, could you play it on fast forward?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps it might played on fast forward. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I recall that this woman on the phone here is a relative of Velija and subsequently there is going to be several people sitting in a living room. There is a picture on the wall, I presume it is Velija. There is Mr. Mucic there and I think that this is subsequent to a funeral. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps it could be played fast forward. Please watch the screen and make sure you have it on your screen. Could you play it fast forward and look at it. If you see any part that you recognise, tell us quickly and we will stop the video at that point, but it is not -- I notice it is not on my television screen at the moment. Could it be fast forwarded? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prior to that there were the images that I referred to, that is to say a picture of a young person on the wall and then if you could play on from that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Play on, please. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember this scene with the woman crying and now shortly, we should be seeing Mr. Mucic in the group. If you could please play on? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What is the witness expecting? We just want to know whether he viewed the tape and if he viewed it, whether these were part of the scenes which he viewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I think the witness has probably seen enough, but he has indicated that there is a scene of Mr. Mucic which is about to come on the screen and for the sake of completeness, unless it be said that it was not shown and any opposition by the Defence, I thought it might be appropriate to wait.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember this scene as well, where one of the men shows a photograph. I take it Velija is on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. I do not think it is necessary to see any more of that particular video. I would now ask you to play the next video, number M1B, which is exhibit number 110. Again, perhaps it could be -- I think if it is played from the start, this may be more successful this time, so could you play it from the start but not at fast forward. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps we could fast forward. If you see a part you recognise, Mr. Panzer, please tell us to stop. Could we fast forward, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: M1B, there was landscapes shown and then there was a parade where Dzemal Delalic and Zejnil Delalic appeared in uniform and this -- this scene, stop, hold it. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember this as well. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you sure this is M1B?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think the wrong tape has been put in the video. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I ask because there is a tape with three references on -- rather licence plates, there are three licence plate numbers, two Viennese and one from Munich and I think that is M1C.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can I ask that it be checked and see what one they put in?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is M1B.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is M1B. Could you continue looking at it and see if there is any part of it that you recognise. Perhaps it should be gone through on fast forward. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember this scene at the cafe with cases of beer and the people there sitting on the chairs in front of the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please proceed to the next video which is marked M1C and given the number Exhibit 111. Could you play that, please, again on fast forward and Mr. Panzer when you see it, if you see any part of it that you recognise, would you please ask for them to stop the video? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hold it. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This looks familiar. This is a scene of the car going through the countryside, there is Konjic in the background. This goes on for quite some time, but this is something I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move to the final tape which is M1D and given the number Exhibit 112. Again could that be played on fast forward to commence with and Mr. Panzer, if there is any part of it that you recognise, would you please ask them to stop the tape. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hold it. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the tape where for an hour and a half you can see Mucic and his friends, fellow soldiers, they are in a room there, there is just one woman there with them and there is some singing and drinking going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. When the tapes are returned from the booth, I tender them, your Honour. No further questions after that, your Honour, after I have dealt with the question of tendering those four tapes. (Handed). I tender those tapes, your Honours, on the basis of establishment of the chain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: They are admitted. In cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour we will proceed in this way. First counsel for Mr. Delalic, second counsel for Mr. Mucic, third counsel for Mr. Delic and fourth counsel for Mr. Landzo. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. O'Sullivan. Cross-examined by MR. O'SULLIVAN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Panzer, I have a few questions for you relating to this matter. To begin, I have a few questions about you. To begin with, you have told us you are a member of Division 1 of the Vienna police department, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, counsel for the Defence, our division is Division 1 or department 1 and is one of five of the police directorate in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In March 1996, you were known as a group leader; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not true. I was leader of a group in May 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your position in March 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was also group leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many years have you been a police officer, in total?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 1974.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that you have had a number of years of training, both practical and theoretical, concerning the handling of physical evidence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the police school and in the detective course we were shown how to deal with these matters of the code for criminal procedure, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your many years of experience, I would assume you have had occasion to seize evidence pursuant to search warrants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, over the years a number of seizures in the execution of orders from the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you just told the Tribunal that you carry out these searches and seizures pursuant to the code of criminal procedure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. The code of criminal procedure states that when you -- on the basis of certain facts, the investigating judge will draw up an order. There can be initiative taken by the police itself. There are provisions in the code that make that sort of procedure, upon very strict criteria.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In all respects regarding the alleged searches of Taubergasse 15 and the premises of INDA-Bau that were carried out pursuant to the code you have just mentioned; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All searches in this case were ordered by Dr Seda, the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were carried out in their entirety pursuant to the code; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The order to carry out a house search was given to us by the investigating judge. The people in Division 1 tried to execute the order in compliance with the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was quite simple: was it carried out in pursuance of the code of criminal procedures; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were two search warrants issued in connection with the arrest of Mr. Mucic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before seeking to have the search warrants issued, you had in your possession registration about the people who were registered as living at Taubergasse 15 in Vienna; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also had information concerning INDA-Bau, such things as the structure, the company, the names of directors, the names of shareholders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to Taubergasse 15, it was your colleague Moerbaur who collected the information on the individuals registered at that address, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, with the assistance of the usher I would like the witness to be shown a document. I have a copy for the witness which I ask be shown to the Prosecution and a copy for each one of your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be marked D62/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Mr. Panzer, I would ask you to have a look at this document. It is in the German language with the English translation attached. I would ask you to look at the German, perhaps. You will see a cover letter dated 15th March 1996, followed by registration information for Taubergasse 15. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is a registration note about all the people who were living at Taubergasse 15 who reported to the police as having been there or still being there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact this document contains both the names of people who are registered and those although are deregistered; in other words no longer living at Taubergasse 15; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the first page, page 1 of the German version, do you have that? The first name there is Sefika Rizvanovic, born 14th December 1939, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says she was registered as living at Taubergasse 15, door 15, since 13th January 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And door 15 is on the second floor next to door 14 at Taubergasse, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not really know exactly where it is. 14 was on the second floor. I do not know whether 15 was next door to it or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that Sefika Rizvanovic is the sister of Zejnil Delalic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says Nee Delalic. Whether it was his sister or not I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you knew she was present the day the alleged search of door 14 took place, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not really know. Hariso Delalic was there, but Sefika, I really do not know. Hariso Delalic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For now I am asking you about Sefika Rizvanovic. Do you know whether she was there that day and whether she was the sister of Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page, page 1 of the German version, the third name down is a Salem Halilhodzic, born 5th July 1942, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He is registered at Taubergasse 15, door 14, living there since 19th October 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew he worked at the BH club located on the ground floor of Taubergasse 15; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew he was present at Taubergasse 15 the day of the alleged search that took place at Taubergasse 15, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page, the next name down is Jasmina Halilhodzic born 12th November 1950, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She is registered as living at Taubergasse 15, door 14, since 11th January 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is it an appropriate time to take a break, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you mind if we have a break and come back at 4.30?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will break. (4.00 pm) (A short break) (4.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you for a few seconds by making an announcement? The Trial Chamber will sit at 11.00 am tomorrow, because of a hospital appointment a member of the Trial Chamber has. We will sit at that time. Thank you. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Officer Panzer, before the break we were looking at the exhibit marked as D62/1 and you recall that this -- you have identified it as the document that contains the names of the people who were registered as living at Taubergasse 15 in the middle of March, March 18th 1996, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is from 18th March, it is true -- it is not from 18th March. This does not necessarily mean though that the people are living in the place that they were reported as living to the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were, in fact, registered as living there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is also the document that accompanied the letter of March 15th 1996 in support of the search warrants; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are talking about this one? Do you mean this one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document we are looking at --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you asking whether this was the basis for the search warrant?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was attached to the letter of March 15th 1996 which is the first page in the bundle you have there. It was attached to that letter of March 15th in support of the issuance of the search warrant. If you go back a page, I think. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really say. I do not know. This piece of paper, I do not think it is something that went to the court, because there was a report of several pages sent to the court of 15th March through Interpol, in which it was stated what was the information for the basis of the search, but I do not think this was the paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I ask you to look at the page just before the one you have in front of you. That is the letter of March 15th to which you make reference. Attached to that letter was this document regarding registration at Taubergasse 15, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You would have to ask Mr. Furst because he was the person who sent this to the district court, not me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are familiar with this document we are looking at regarding registration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first page is not mine. That was written by one of my colleagues, the registration information. That is not something I did. That was produced by Interpol, by Mr. Furst, the administrative officer there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the question is, you are familiar with the pages that follow, the pages that list the names of the people registered at Taubergasse 15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with those. I recognise them. It was the Tuesday or the Wednesday that I gave documents to Mr. Furst and I would assume that he used those and that then he was in contact -- Interpol was in contact with the district court, but it is not something that I produced myself or sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I draw your attention to the first page of the registration, the one we were looking at before the break. I ask you to find the name Ines Halilhodzic, born 30th August 1970, can you see that there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This person is shown as registered as living at Taubergasse 15, door 14, since 11th January 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next name down is Damir Halilhodzic born 28th January 1977?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
